questions.prompt: Where is Ciudad Juárez, the border city that Orozco and Villa took in May 1911? Click the map.
questions.explanation: Against Madero's orders, Orozco and Villa attacked the federal garrison across the river from El Paso, and General Juan Navarro surrendered on 10 May. It was the first major city taken by the rebels and gave Madero a port of entry on the US border.

questions.prompt: Under the Treaty of Ciudad Juárez of May 1911, who was to serve as interim president until elections?
options: Francisco León de la Barra
Ramón Corral
Eulalio Gutiérrez
Adolfo de la Huerta
questions.explanation: Díaz and Vice President Corral were to resign, and Díaz's foreign minister, León de la Barra, would hold office until elections. The treaty left the federal army and the Porfirian state in place, which many revolutionaries, Zapata among them, came to see as Madero's fatal mistake.

questions.prompt: Breaking with Madero in November 1911, what did Zapata's Plan of Ayala demand?
options: The return of lands, woods and waters taken by the haciendas
The restoration of constitutional rule, with nothing on land
A national rising on 20 November against Díaz's re-election
National ownership of the subsoil and its oil
questions.explanation: The plan declared Madero a traitor and also called for the expropriation, with compensation, of a third of the great estates. It remained the Zapatista programme for the rest of the decade; the Convention of Aguascalientes adopted its principles in 1914.

questions.prompt: During the Decena Trágica of February 1913, which general, commanding the government's forces, had Madero arrested and took power?
options: Victoriano Huerta
Bernardo Reyes
Pascual Orozco
Joaquín Beltrán
questions.explanation: While the rebels and government forces shelled each other across the city centre, Huerta negotiated with the rebels and the US ambassador, Henry Lane Wilson, and agreed with Félix Díaz in the "Pact of the Embassy" to take power. Madero and Pino Suárez were shot beside the Lecumberri penitentiary on the night of 22 February.

questions.prompt: In April 1914 US sailors and marines seized Veracruz to stop a German ship landing arms for Huerta. Where is Veracruz? Click the map.
questions.explanation: Cadets of the Naval School and townspeople resisted, and many more Mexicans than Americans were killed. The occupation cut Huerta off from his main customs house, and when US forces left in November 1914 Carranza made the port his capital.

questions.prompt: Carranza's Constitutionalist zone of December 1914 looked small on a map. How did he pay for the arms to fight Villa and Zapata?
options: Gulf customs, oil taxes and henequen
Northern cattle and cotton sold to the US
Sugar from the haciendas of Morelos
Silver from the mines of Zacatecas
questions.explanation: From Veracruz he held the Gulf coast from the lower Rio Grande to Yucatán, and with it the customs revenue of Veracruz and Tampico, the oil taxes and the henequen of Yucatán. Villa, who held Zacatecas and paid for arms with the north's cattle, cotton and mines, never held a Gulf port or the oil zone.

questions.prompt: How did Obregón break Villa's División del Norte at Celaya in April 1915?
options: He dug in behind trenches, wire and machine guns
He surprised Villa with a captured coal train
He stormed the hills of La Bufa and El Grillo
He cut Villa's coal supply on the railway
questions.explanation: Villa's cavalry wore itself out in frontal charges on 6–7 April, and when Villa attacked again on 13–15 April he was routed by Obregón's reserve cavalry striking his flanks. The two battles broke the División del Norte's offensive power and turned the war in Carranza's favour.

questions.prompt: What brought General Pershing's US army into Chihuahua in March 1916?
options: Villa's raid on Columbus, New Mexico
The arrest of US sailors at Tampico
A German ship bringing arms for Huerta
The clash with Carrancistas at Carrizal
questions.explanation: About 10,000 US troops pushed south from Colonia Dublán as far as Parral without catching Villa. After clashes with Carrancista troops at Parral and Carrizal they fell back, and the expedition left Mexico in February 1917.

questions.prompt: Where is Querétaro, where a Constituent Congress wrote the Constitution of 1917? Click the map.
questions.explanation: Going beyond Carranza's draft, the Congress vested ownership of land, waters and the subsoil in the nation (Article 27), set labour rights (Article 123) and made education secular (Article 3). Promulgated on 5 February 1917, the constitution is still in force.

questions.prompt: In the Plan of Agua Prieta of 1920, the Sonoran leaders disowned Carranza and backed whom?
options: Álvaro Obregón
Ignacio Bonillas
Pancho Villa
Pablo González
questions.explanation: Carranza had tried to impose a civilian successor, Ignacio Bonillas, and sent troops into Sonora. Most of the army joined the plan within weeks; Carranza fled the capital and was killed at Tlaxcalantongo, and Obregón was elected that autumn.
